# `path-param-renamed`

Path parameter renamed (same endpoint)

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `sdk` |
| **Default severity** | `info` · `--profile sdk`: `warn` |
| **Rule IDs** | `path-param-renamed` |
| **Status** | Implemented (M3) |
| **Group** | Paths and operations ([RULES.md section 2](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

A path parameter was renamed in the same position, e.g. `/users/{id}` → `/users/{userId}`. The endpoint is the same.

## Why this default

The URL clients call is unchanged, but SDKs that name method arguments after parameters change their signatures.

## Example

From test case [`path-param-renamed`](../../test/cases/path-param-renamed/): Renaming a path parameter keeps the same endpoint.

`openapi.yaml`, base → revision:

```diff
  …
    version: 1.0.0
  paths:
-   '/pets/{id}':
+   '/pets/{petId}':
      get:
        parameters:
-       - name: id
+       - name: petId
          in: path
          required: true
```

Findings:

- `path-param-renamed` · info · GET /pets/{petId}

## Test cases

The example above is the only test case for this rule.


## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file. The policy file arrives in M6; see [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml
rules:
  path-param-renamed: info
```

## How to fix

Keep the old parameter name unless the SDK change is intended.
